newsitem.title: GERMANY: German unity cost 200 bln marks a year -institute.
newsitem.headline: German unity cost 200 bln marks a year -institute.

text.p: German unification has cost a net 200 billion marks a year since 1990, or around six percent of pan-German gross domestic product, the RWI economic research institute said on Friday.

The Essen-based think-tank, one of Germany's six leading economic institutes, said transfers to the former communist east German states have cost the affluent west seven percent of its total annual economic output since unification.
"The costs will remain the same, around five percent of GDP, at least until the end of the decade," RWI said in a study on the costs of German unification.

The German government has financed the huge price tag for healing the economic wounds after 40 years of communist rule through taxes, around 43 percent of the total, and cuts in state spending, around 15 percent, and borrowing.
The most controversial form of financing has been the so-called "solidarity tax", a 7.5 percent surcharge on income tax bills.

The west German economy benefitted initially from a boom in consumer demand immediately after the Berlin Wall was toppled in 1989. But rising tax burdens and spending cuts later hit individuals and businesses and was felt particularly hard in 1995, RWI said.

The trend could be changed if west Germany were able to kick-start its sluggish economy, it added. The sooner dynamic changes are made in west Germany the less unification will cost when the final bill comes in.
